questions.question: Mohan covers a distance of 187 km at the speed of S km/hr. If Mohan increases his speed by 6 km/hr, then he takes 6 hours less. What is the value of S?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance = 187 km

Initial speed = S km/hr

New speed = (S + 6) km/hr

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Let the Initial time be x hours

∴ New time = (x - 6) hours

We know,

Sx = 187 km

(S + 6) (x - 6) = 187 km

⇒ Sx - 6S + 6x - 36 = 187

⇒ 187 - 6S + 6x - 36 = 187 (∵ Sx = 187 km)

⇒ 6x - 6S = 36

⇒ x - S = 6 ---(1)

We know,

Sx = 187 km

⇒ x = 187/S ---(2)

Substitute (2) in (1)

⇒ (187/S) - S = 6

⇒ (187 - S²)/S = 6

⇒ S² + 6S - 187 = 0

⇒ S2 - 11S + 17S - 187 = 0

⇒ S(S - 11) + 17(S - 11) = 0

⇒ (S - 11) (S + 17) = 0

∴ S = 11 or S = -17

Speed never be negative

∴ S = 11 km/hr

questions.question: A 250 metre long train takes 30 seconds to cross a 350 metres long bridge. How much time train will take to cross a 550 metre long bridge?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the Train = 250 m

Length of the first Bridge = 350 m

Length of the second Bridge = 550 m

Time taken to cross = 30 s

**Concept:**

Speed of the Train will be the same while crossing both the two Bridges

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculation:**

First we have to calculate the speed of the Train

While crossing the first Bridge,

Total distance = Length of Train + Length of Bridge

⇒ Total distance = (250 + 350) = 600 m

⇒ Speed of the Train = 600/30 = 20 m/s

Now, while crossing the second Bridge,

Total distance = Length of Train + Length of Bridge

⇒ Total distance = (250 + 550) = 800 m

Time = Total distance/Speed of the Train

⇒ Time taken to cross the Bridge of length 550 m = 800/20 = 40 seconds

questions.question: If C alone can complete two-third part of a work in 12 days, then in how many days C can complete the whole work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

C alone can complete two-third part of a work in 12 days

**Concept:**

If a person can complete (x/y) part of a work in z days, then the person can complete the whole work in {z × (y/x)} days

**Calculation:**

2/3 part → 12 days

⇒ 1 part → 12 × (3/2) = 18 days

∴ C can complete the whole work in 18 days

questions.question: P sells an article to Q at a loss of 5% and Q sells that article to R at a loss of 20%. If R pays ₹ 2812 for the article, then what was the cost price for P?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P sells an article to Q at a loss of 5%

Q sells that article to R at a loss of 20%

R pays ₹ 2812 for the article

**Concept:**

P sells the article to Q. Therefore Q's Cost Price will be P's Selling Price and Q sells the article to R. Therefore R's Cost Price will be Q's Selling Price

**Calculation:**

R pays ₹ 2812 for the article

∴ R's Cost Price = 2812

Q's Selling Price = R's Cost Price = 2812

⇒ Q's Cost Price = 2812 × (100/80) = 3515 (∵ 20% Loss)

P's Selling Price = Q's Cost Price = 3515

⇒ P's Cost Price = 3515 × (100/95) = 3700 (∵ 5% Loss)

∴ The cost price for P = ₹3700

questions.question: In an Election between Ravi and Manoj, Ravi gets 61% of the total valid votes. If the total votes were 25000 and 20% of the total votes were declared invalid, then other candidate Manoj gets how many numbers of votes?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ravi gets 61% of the total valid votes

Total votes = 25000 

20% of the total votes were declared invalid

**Calculation:**

Total votes = 25000 

⇒ Invalid votes = 20% of 25000 = 5000

⇒ Valid votes = 25000 - 5000 = 20000

Ravi gets 61% of the total valid votes

⇒ Manoj gets 39% of the total valid votes

∴ Number of votes Manoj gets = 20000 × (39/100) = 7800

questions.question: If cost price of an article is ₹ 928 and profit % is 15%, then what will be the net profit?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost Price = 928

Profit % = 15 %

**Concept:**

Profit % is calculated on Cost Price unless it is specified Profit on Selling Price

**Formula used:**

Profit % = (Profit/Cost Price) × 100

**Calculation:**

P % = (P/C.P) × 100

⇒ 15 = (P/928) × 100

⇒ P = (15 × 928)/100 = 139.20

∴ The net profit = ₹ 139.20

questions.question: Simple interest for three years for a certain sum at the rate of 15% is ₹ 9000. If the rate of interest becomes 30%, then what will be the simple interest for two years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective interest percentage = Rate × Time.

Case 1 effective interest = 15% × 3 = 45%.

Case 2 effective interest = 30% × 2 = 60%.

Here, 45% of the principal corresponds to ₹9000.

⇒ Required Simple Interest (60%) = (9000 ÷ 45) × 60 = 200 × 60 = 12000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Simple Interest (SI₁) = ₹ 9000

Initial Rate (R₁) = 15% and Time (T₁) = 3 years

New Rate (R₂) = 30% and Time (T₂) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 Principal (P)
 
 

 
 Case 1: 15% for 3 yrs
 SI = 45% of P
 
•

 Case 2: 30% for 2 yrs
 SI = 60% of P
 
• 
 ? = ₹ 12000

**Calculations:**

⇒ 9000 = (P × 15 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 9000 = (P × 45) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (9000 × 100) ÷ 45

⇒ P = 200 × 100 = ₹ 20000

Now, calculating new Simple Interest (SI₂):

⇒ SI₂ = (20000 × 30 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = 20000 × 60 ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = 200 × 60

⇒ SI₂ = 12000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Interest Rate Concept

For Simple Interest, the effective rate applied over the entire period is simply the product of Rate and Time (R × T). Setting up a direct proportion using effective percentages often saves calculation time.

Simple vs Compound Interest

While SI is calculated only on the initial principal for all years, CI is calculated on the accumulated amount. The difference for 2 years between CI and SI can be found using: D = P(R/100)².

questions.question: The average monthly expenditure of a family is ₹ 8160 for the first 2 months, ₹ 12780 for the next 5 months and ₹ 14280 for the last 5 months. If the family saves ₹ 66300 in the whole year, then what will be the average monthly income of the family?

₹ 12780 for next 5 months

Total Expenditure = Average Expenditure × Number of Months

Income = Expenditure + Savings

**Calculation:**

Total Expenditure for the next 5 months = 12780 × 5 = 63900

Total Expenditure for the last 5 months = 14280 × 5 = 71400

∴ Total Expenditure for 1 year = 16320 + 63900 + 71400 = 151620

Total Savings for 1 year = 66300 

⇒ Total income for 1 year = 151620 + 66300 = 217920

∴ The average monthly income of the family = 217920/12 = ₹18160

questions.question: If (1)/(A):(1)/(B):(1)/(C) = 2 : 3 :4, then what is the ratio of A : B : C?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

(1)/(A):(1)/(B):(1)/(C) = 2 : 3 :4

**Calculation:**

Let (1/A) = 2x, (1/B) = 3x, and (1/C) = 4x

⇒ A = (1/2x), B = (1/3x), and C = (1/4x)

Now, LCM (2x, 3x, 4x) = 24x

On multiplying each term by 24x,

A : B : C = (24x/2x) : (24x/3x) : (24x/4x)

⇒ A : B : C = 12 : 8 : 6 = 6 : 4 : 3

**∴ The ratio of A : B : C is 6 : 4 : 3.**

**Calculation:**

Total sum of A = 3 + 4 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 0 = 10

Total sum of B = 2 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 10

Middle value of 0 - 2 = 1

Middle value of 2 - 4 = 3

Middle value of 4 - 6 = 5

Middle value of 6 - 8 = 7

Middle value of 8 - 10 = 9

Middle value of 10 - 12 = 11

Now,

Multiplying these values with values of A = (1 × 3) + (3 × 4) + (5 × 1) + (7 × 1) + (9 × 1) + (11 × 0) = 36

Multiplying these values with values of B = (1 × 2) + (3 × 1) + (5 × 3) + (7 × 1) + (9 × 1) + (11 × 2) = 58

⇒ Total of A + B = 36 + 58 = 94

∴ Combined mean of A and B = 94/(10 + 10) = 4.7

questions.question: What will be the least Common Multiple of 2² × 3⁵ × 7³ and 2⁴ × 3⁴ × 7¹?
questions.solution:
**Concept:**

LCM is the product of Prime factors with highest power

**Explanation:**

Here, the Prime factors are:

2² × 3⁵ × 7³

2⁴ × 3⁴ × 7¹

Highest power for 2 is 2⁴

Highest power for 3 is 3⁵

Highest power for 7 is 7³

∴ LCM = 2⁴ × 3⁵ × 7³

questions.question: Marked price of an article is 70% more than its cost price. After giving a discount of 10%, article is sold for ₹ 1071. What will be the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price of an article is 70% more than its cost price

Discount = 10%

Selling Price = 1071

**Concept:**

Discount is always gives on Marked Price

**Formula used:**

Selling Price = Marked Price - Discount

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price be x

⇒ Marked Price = x + (x × (70/100)) = 1.7x

⇒ Discount = 1.7x × (10/100) = 0.17x

⇒ Selling Price = 1.7x - 0.17x = 1.53x

Now,

1.53x = 1071

⇒ x = 1071/1.53 = 700

∴ Cost Price of the Article = ₹ 700

**Alternate Method:**

Let C.P be 100

⇒ M.P = 170

⇒ Discount = 17

⇒ S.P = 170 - 17 = 153

Now, 

153 → 1071

100 → (1071/153) × 100 = 700

∴ Cost Price of the Article = ₹ 700
